title: Ordnance Quality Assurance/Safety Observer (MGySgt to Cpl) NMOS (6048, 6282, 6286, 6287, 6288 6531, 6541, 6591), DC AVN
raw_text:
2. MOS 6516, Ordnance Quality Assurance/Safety Observer (MGySgt to Cpl) NMOS
(6048, 6282, 6286, 6287, 6288 6531, 6541, 6591), DC AVN

    a. Summary. Aviation ordnance, flight equipment, or Aircraft Safety
Mechanic Quality Assurance/Safety Observers (QA/SO’s) assigned to
organizational, intermediate level work centers, station weapons, and Marine
Training Units (schoolhouses) shall monitor and enforce safe handling of
explosives and adherence to established procedures during all explosive
ordnance evolutions. QA/SO’s are responsible to the Commanding Officer and
are qualified/certified by the designated Ordnance Officer via By Direction
authority. At the Organizational level, Aviation Ordnance QA/SO’s supervise
weapons inspections, loading, downloading and storage of ancillary explosive
components as well as the build-up of electronic countermeasures related to
the T/M/S of their assigned unit. Flight Equipment QA/SO’s supervise the
inspection, maintenance, and repair of applicable aircrew survival equipment,
while Aircraft Safety Mechanic QA/SO’s supervise the inspection, maintenance,
and repair of aircraft centered safety equipment and systems. At the
intermediate level and station weapons, Aviation Ordnance QA/SO’s supervise
the breakout, buildup/ assembly, testing & programming, delivery & receipt,
storage, and logistical efforts for all weapons associated with the T/M/S
flying squadrons they support, while Flight Equipment QA/SO’s supervise the
inspection, maintenance, and repair of aircrew life support systems.

       b.    Prerequisites

        (1) 65xx: MOS 65xx formal schools training, explosive handlers
physical, and arms, ammunition & explosives (AA&E) screening.

        (2) 6048 or 628X: Completion of naval explosives safety for
supervisors & managers (AMMO-49-DL), explosive handler’s physical, and arms,
ammunition, and explosives (AA&E) screening.

    c. Requirements. Previously qualified and certified as a team leader,
successfully complete the applicable QASO qualification/certification
syllabus, and designated as a QASO by the qualification/certification board
chairman upon the successful completion of a qualification/certification
board.


                                         3-420                   Enclosure (1)
 3143                                                                  NAVMC 1200.1L



    d. Duties. For a listing of duties and tasks, refer to reference (bo),
Aviation Training and Readiness Program Manual.

    e.      Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
None.

       f.   Related Military Skill.     None.
common_text: Aviation Ordnance MOSs handle Class V(A) ammunition issues from safety to procurement, storage, buildup, delivery, and subsequent aircraft loading and downloading. The OccFld includes both organizational and intermediate maintenance of aircraft weapon systems, aircraft guns, gun pods, aircraft crew-served weapons, bomb racks, missile launchers, and armament weapons support equipment (AWSE). Aviation Ordnance Marines are qualified and certified to handle Class V(A) munitions under current directives. Formal schooling is provided to Marines entering the OccFld. A wide variety of billet assignments are available as shown in the figure later in this entry. Marines entering the OccFld receive MOS 6500, Basic Aviation Ordnance Marine, and attend Aviation Ordnance, Class AO A1 School (N23G3U2) at Pensacola, Fl., with follow-on training at one of several CNATT AO(C) courses, dependent upon anticipated fleet assignment. Upon completion of the applicable AO(C) course, they are designated as either MOS 6531 Aircraft Ordnance Technician or MOS 6541 Aviation Ordnance Systems Technician and are assigned to a T/M/S flying squadron in the case of MOS 6531 or a Marine Aviation Logistics Squadron(MALS)/Station Weapons in the case of MOS 6541.

matches: Maintain, repair, and rebuild aircraft structures, functional components, and parts, such as wings and fuselage, rigging, hydraulic units, oxygen systems, fuel systems, electrical systems, gaskets, or seals.

The OccFld includes both organizational and intermediate maintenance of aircraft weapon systems, aircraft guns, gun pods, aircraft crew-served weapons, bomb racks, missile launchers, and armament weapons support equipment (AWSE).
Inspect facilities, machinery, or safety equipment to identify and correct potential hazards, and to ensure safety regulation compliance.

Aviation ordnance, flight equipment, or Aircraft Safety Mechanic Quality Assurance/Safety Observers (QA/SO’s) assigned to organizational, intermediate level work centers, station weapons, and Marine Training Units (schoolhouses) shall monitor and enforce safe handling of explosives and adherence to established procedures during all explosive ordnance evolutions.
Inform supervisors of equipment malfunctions that need to be addressed.

At the Organizational level, Aviation Ordnance QA/SO’s supervise weapons inspections, loading, downloading and storage of ancillary explosive components as well as the build-up of electronic countermeasures related to the T/M/S of their assigned unit.
Inspect new, repaired, or modified aircraft to identify damage or defects and to assess airworthiness and conformance to standards, using checklists, hand tools, and test instruments.

Flight Equipment QA/SO’s supervise the inspection, maintenance, and repair of applicable aircrew survival equipment, while Aircraft Safety Mechanic QA/SO’s supervise the inspection, maintenance, and repair of aircraft centered safety equipment and systems.
Attend preflight briefings concerning weather, altitudes, routes, emergency procedures, crew coordination, lengths of flights, food and beverage services offered, and numbers of passengers.
For a listing of duties and tasks, refer to reference (bo), Aviation Training and Readiness Program Manual.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
